newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Glaverbel sees 1997 sales, op profit up.
newsitem.headline: Glaverbel sees 1997 sales, op profit up.

text.p: The head of Belgian glass group Glaverbel said on Wednesday prices had begun to move upwards, leaving the group optimistic on 1997 results.

"Higher sales and improved operating results are forecast for the group in 1997, thanks to the special types of glass developed and marketed by it, and thanks also to the full utilisation of production capacity," Glaverbel chief executive officer Luc Willame told the company's annual general meeting.
A text of his comments was made avaialable by the company.

The good level of shipments during the second half of 1996 continued into 1997. While prices were still depressed at the start of the year they nevertheless began to move upwards during the month of April," Willame said.
Willame said the group was also examining "several investment opportunities at international level, in line with its policy of geographical expansion."
A thin glass processing plant set up in southern China last year should start in June, he said.

Willame said Glaverbel's raw glass, achitectural glass and automotive divisions were all working on new products. Repair work being undertaken at the group's Maasglas float, one of seven in the group, should permit geographic optimisation of production capacity, he said.
Glaverbel sales rose one percent in 1996 to 38.663 billion Belgian francs. Operating profit fell 8.5 percent to 2.732 billion francs against the background of falling glass prices.
Net profit more than doubled to 1.915 billion francs, thanks to 606 million francs in capital gains, mainly on the sale of its stake in U.S. glass maker AFG to Asahi Glass Co.
Japan's Asahi Glass is Glaverbel's majority shareholder.
